views.markdown:
**iosc** is the Wayland compositor every Xios desktop runs on. It's a small compositor I wrote on libwayland-server. It composites windows on the Apple GPU through ANGLE and Metal and hands the finished frame to the Xios app over a shared IOSurface, so nothing is copied per frame.

With **iosc-shell** it is the iosc desktop. KDE runs KWin nested inside it, and the native flavor uses it to put each Linux app in its own iPadOS window.

- xdg-shell windows and popups, layer-shell, subsurfaces, viewporter, fractional scale, and clipboard
- Touch, Pencil, keyboard, mouse and trackpad input from the Xios app
- X11 apps through rootless Xwayland: the X window manager is built in and stays off unless `IOSC_XWAYLAND` is set. `xios-session` sets it when Xwayland is installed (the **xios-x11** flavor), and each desktop slot gets its own X display
- Ships `run-iosc.sh`, a paint self-test that needs no other app, and `run-kgx.sh`, which opens GNOME Console

You normally don't install this directly. Every flavor pulls it in.

The compositor is signed with the graphics entitlements it needs for GPU access; a copy of that entitlement file is installed under `/var/jb/usr/local/share/iosc` for reference.

## 0.9.51  ·  2026-10-25
- X11 windows actually show up now: the window manager asks Xwayland to redirect top-level windows, which rootless Xwayland needs before it makes a Wayland surface for them
- X windows without an alpha channel draw opaque instead of see-through
- iosc picks the X display for each desktop slot, so a second slot's Xwayland gets :1 instead of taking over :0

## 0.9.50  ·  2026-10-25
- Builds the rootless Xwayland window manager by default (it stays off until `IOSC_XWAYLAND` is set)
- Fixes a start-up deadlock that kept the window manager from ever starting
- Starts Xwayland without MIT-SHM, which iOS can't provide

## 0.8.0  ·  2026-06-30
- First release: clean-room Wayland compositor that composites clients on the Apple GPU into the Xios app's shared image
- xdg-shell windows and popups, subsurfaces, viewporter, fractional scale, and clipboard
- Multiple windows with stacking and focus on tap; touch and keyboard routed into the focused window
- Runs GTK4 and GNOME apps (validated with GNOME Console and a live shell) on the A10 GPU
- Includes run-iosc.sh (paint self-test) and run-kgx.sh (GNOME Console launcher)
